subject: BurstAlley p99 latency surge — ops coordination, short-term mitigations, and customer update
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, k.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: BurstAlley p99 latency spike — initial triage and asks

Team —

We started seeing a sustained p99 response-time jump for BurstAlley’s gen-api starting ~15:45 UTC. Impact: 5–8x p99 on their production fleet, throughput nominal but many client requests timing out at the tail. BurstAlley reports increased customer errors (they pinged Ops). I pulled the quick metrics — attaching CSV with short windows and traces.

Immediate asks:
- SRE: can you validate whether this is queue-throttling (kernel/dispatch) or a runtime tail spike (KV cache evaporation) — key signals: kernel queue depth, per-GPU scheduler backlog, and cache hit rates.
- Marissa / Prod: can you confirm whether any recent rollout to gen-api variants or routing-policy changes for BA happened last 24h?
- Ben: can we pre-check whether routing fallbacks to the lower-latency model variant are enabled for this customer? If not, can we enable a temporary fallback policy?

Customer comm: Asha at BurstAlley has asked for an ETA. We should have a short holding note within 60 minutes and a more detailed update within 3 hours. I started a PagerDuty incident (PD-78923).

Attachments: incident_metrics_20280514.csv (short window token/latency snapshot)

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, k.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 16:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BurstAlley p99 latency spike — initial triage and asks

On Tue, 14 May 2028 at 16:12, Grace O'Connor wrote:
> We started seeing a sustained p99 response-time jump for BurstAlley’s gen-api starting ~15:45 UTC.

Quick update — triage in progress. Early signals:
- Kernel queue depth on the affected pool is elevated (~2.5x normal) but not saturated.
- KV cache hit-rate for the primary shard dropped from 92% -> 61% around 15:44 UTC.
- We see a correlated spike in long GC pauses on the memory manager on node gpu-13 in pool-west-2.

Hypothesis: a combination of cache churn and one noisy node leading to amplification of tail latency. Long GC pauses cause token generation stalls; the scheduler queues up and pushes p99.

Short-term mitigation being executed now:
1) Remove node gpu-13 from rotation (drain) — in progress.
2) Toggle aggressive prefix/KV cache retention to preserve warms for BurstAlley’s route (config change) — applying.
3) If we still see p99 > 2s after 15 minutes, we recommend enabling a fallback to the small-quantized model variant for BurstAlley (nonbreaking by policy).

We’ll post a customer-facing holding note once drains and cache tweak are applied (ETA: 20–25m).

— SRE on-call (shared mailbox)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>, k.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BurstAlley p99 latency spike — initial triage and asks

Thanks for the fast triage. Quick notes from product:
- No recent route or model rollout targeted at BurstAlley in last 48h. Canary metrics look green.
- We did push a minor KV eviction threshold tweak globally yesterday for mem-opt across low-priority pools — will check whether BurstAlley’s shards overlapped that policy.

Product asks / guidance for the mitigation window:
1) If SRE enables fallback to the smaller quant model, document the expected output delta (we expect minimal quality regression on short prompts but validate with sample set).
2) For a 3-hour timeline: we need a short RCA note draft (2–3 bullets) and a triage log to share with customer and internal leadership.
3) Request for eng: can we prioritize a deeper look into GC and runtime memory compaction behavior for the memory manager, this looks like repeat behavior we saw in Feb.

I’ll help with the customer note once SRE gives the state of mitigations.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BurstAlley p99 latency spike — initial triage and asks

Updating routing policy status:
- BurstAlley is on a strict routing map but we have an emergency override to allow fallback to model-quant-sm (compatible interface) for incidents. Setting override now (should be live in ~3 minutes).
- I’ll also temporarily bump their capacity on the dedicated pool by +10% to reduce queueing while drain completes. That is non-permanent, we'll roll it back once stable.

Draft customer holding note (proposed; short):
"Hi Asha — we’re seeing an elevated tail latency on your gen-api traffic. Our on-call team is draining a noisy node and applying cache retention changes now; we expect a material reduction in p99 within 30 minutes. We’ll follow with a full status update in ~3 hours. — Grace, Redwood Inference"

Attaching quick CSV export of the short window for reference (incident_metrics_20280514.csv).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Verma <asha@burstalley.com>
Cc: BurstAlley Ops <ops@burstalley.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, k.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 17:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: BurstAlley p99 latency spike — ops update

Hi Asha — quick update from Redwood: thanks for flagging this. Our on-call team has identified a noisy node contributing to tail latency and is actively draining it; we’re also applying a cache retention tweak targeted at your route. We have enabled an emergency fallback to a compatible, smaller quantized model to reduce tail latency if needed (we prefer not to use it unless necessary).

What to expect now:
- Short holding: we expect most customer-visible p99 to drop within ~30 minutes as we finish the drain and cache tweaks.
- Follow-up: a detailed status and next steps within 3 hours.

We’ll keep you posted and will share the short RCA afterwards.

If you see anything new on your side (increase in errors, changes to traffic patterns), please reply here.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
